parts.label: (a)

markscheme_points.text: (electric) force is (directly) proportional to product of charges
force (between point charges) is inversely proportional to the square of their separation

hints: Hint 1: Think about what two things control how strongly two point charges push or pull on each other - the size of the charges and how far apart they are.
Hint 2: Remember how the force changes if you double a charge compared to if you double the distance - one is linear, the other is a square law.
parts.proper_answer: The electric force between two point charges is directly proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of their separation.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What Coulomb's Law Describes**
You have two tiny point charges sitting in space. They exert an electric force on each other along the line joining them. The size of that force depends on just two things: how much charge there is, and how far apart they are.

Step 2: **Putting It Into Words**
If you make either charge bigger, the force grows in direct proportion. So force is proportional to $Q_1 Q_2$. If you move them further apart, the force falls off much faster, as one over distance squared. In symbols: $$F = \frac{Q_1 Q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 r^2}$$ but in words you need both the product part and the inverse-square part for full marks.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.part_stem:
Positronium is a system in which an electron and a positron orbit, with the same period, around their common centre of mass, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1}}

Fig. 2.1 (not to scale)

The radius $r$ of the orbit of both particles is $1.59 \times 10^{-10}\text{m}$.
parts.text: Explain how the electric force between the electron and the positron causes the path of the moving particles to be circular.

markscheme_points.text: (electric) force is perpendicular to velocity (of particles)
force (perpendicular to velocity) causes centripetal acceleration or force does not change the speed of the particles or force has constant magnitude

hints: Hint 1: Look at Fig. 2.1 and think about the direction of the attraction between the opposite charges compared to the direction each particle is moving.
Hint 2: Recall what happens when a resultant force acts at 90 degrees to velocity - does it speed the object up or just change its direction?
parts.proper_answer: The electric attraction acts perpendicular to the velocity of each particle, providing the centripetal force. It changes direction without changing speed, with constant magnitude, giving circular motion.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Direction of the Electric Force**
The electron is negative and the positron is positive, so they attract each other. At any instant they are on opposite sides of the circle, so the pull on each one points straight inward toward the centre of the circle. The velocity is along the tangent, so the force is perpendicular to velocity.

Step 2: **Why This Gives a Circle**
A force perpendicular to velocity does no work, so it cannot change speed, only direction. Because the separation stays the same, the magnitude $F$ stays constant. A constant-magnitude force always pointing to the centre is exactly a centripetal force, so each particle keeps bending round in uniform circular motion.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the magnitude of the electric force between the electron and the positron is $2.28 \times 10^{-9}\text{N}$.
hints: Hint 1: Be careful with the separation to use in Coulomb's law - $r$ is the radius of each orbit from the centre, so what is the electron-to-positron distance?
Hint 2: Check the charges to use and the constants: each particle has magnitude $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ and $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \text{ F m}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Finding the True Separation**
$r = 1.59 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ is from the centre to each particle. The electron and positron are on opposite sides, so the distance between them is: $$x = 2r = 2 \times 1.59 \times 10^{-10} = 3.18 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$$ This is a very common slip, so always sketch the two radii end to end.

Step 2: **Applying Coulomb's Law**
Both have charge magnitude $e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$: $$F = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 x^2}$$ $$F = \frac{(1.60 \times 10^{-19})^2}{4\pi \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times (3.18 \times 10^{-10})^2}$$ $$F = 2.28 \times 10^{-9} \text{ N}$$ This inward attraction is what provides the centripetal force in the next part.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Use the information in **(b)(ii)** to determine the period of the circular orbit of the two particles.

markscheme_points.text: $F = mr\omega^2$ and $\omega = 2\pi / T$ or $F = mv^2 / r$ and $v = 2\pi r / T$

hints: Hint 1: The electric force you just found is the only inward force, so think about which circular-motion equation links force, mass, radius and rotation rate.
Hint 2: You are asked for period $T$, so recall how angular speed $\omega$ or linear speed $v$ is linked to $T$ for one full circle.
Hint 3: Rearrange to make $T$ the subject before putting numbers in, using $m_e = 9.11 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$ and orbit radius $r$ (not $2r$).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Equating Electric Force to Centripetal Force**
For each particle the electric force $F$ is the centripetal force: $$F = m r \omega^2$$ with $m = 9.11 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$ and $r = 1.59 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$. Note we use $r$ here because that is the radius of the circular path about the centre.

Step 2: **Introducing the Period**
Angular speed and period are linked by: $$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}$$ Substituting gives: $$F = \frac{4\pi^2 m r}{T^2}$$ Rearranged for $T$: $$T = \sqrt{\frac{4\pi^2 m r}{F}}$$

Step 3: **Calculating the Value**
$$T = \sqrt{\frac{4\pi^2 \times 9.11 \times 10^{-31} \times 1.59 \times 10^{-10}}{2.28 \times 10^{-9}}}$$ $$T = 1.58 \times 10^{-15} \text{ s}$$ This extremely short time makes sense for atomic-scale motion at huge speeds.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem: Positronium is highly unstable, and after a very short period of time it becomes gamma radiation.
parts.text: Describe how gamma radiation is formed from the two particles in positronium.

markscheme_points.text: mass of the electron and positron converted into photon energy

hints: Hint 1: Think about the relationship between an electron and a positron - what special name is given to such a pair?
Hint 2: Recall what happens when matter meets its corresponding antimatter - do they survive or disappear?
Hint 3: If the mass of both particles disappears, think about where that mass goes using $E = mc^2$ and what type of photon is energetic enough.
parts.proper_answer: The positron is the antiparticle of the electron. They undergo pair annihilation, with their total mass converted into energy of gamma photons.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Particle and Antiparticle Meet**
A positron looks just like an electron in mass, but has opposite charge $+e$. It is the antiparticle of the electron. When they are bound so closely in positronium they will interact directly.

Step 2: **Annihilation Into Radiation**
Particle plus antiparticle cannot survive together. They undergo pair annihilation: both masses vanish and all their mass-energy plus kinetic energy is converted into electromagnetic energy, as required by $E = mc^2$.

Step 3: **Why Gamma Photons**
Because the electron rest energy is about $0.511 \text{ MeV}$, the photons created are very high energy, so they are gamma photons, usually two photons emitted to conserve momentum and energy.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State **one** medical application of the process described in **(c)(i)**.
hints: Hint 1: Think of a hospital imaging technique that uses a tracer which emits positrons so that annihilation gamma rays can be detected outside the body.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Medical Use of Annihilation**
In a PET scan a patient is given a tracer that emits positrons. Each positron annihilates with an electron in tissue, producing two gamma photons back-to-back. Detectors around the patient locate where the gamma rays came from, building an image of metabolic activity.
